overview.description: Fast Track is a high-energy North American race game that combines card-driven movement with a physical board of marbles or pegs. Similar in spirit to Sorry! or Ludo, Fast Track replaces dice with each player's personal deck of cards. The goal is to navigate all four marbles around the track and into a central Home Base. The game features strategic mechanics like backwards-moving 4s, split 7s (move two marbles), and a dangerous central shortcut called the 'Fast Track' that saves board space but leaves marbles vulnerable.

history.origins: Fast Track descends from the Aggravation and Wahoo family of race games, which themselves were adaptations of the English game Ludo. The card-based movement system emerged in the late 20th century as a DIY and homemade variant popular in Midwestern USA and Canada.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Board games like Aggravation popularize the 'bump' mechanic (sending opponent pieces back to start).
1970s-1980s: Homemade wooden-board versions using cards emerge, particularly in Midwest and Canada.
1990s-2000s: Fast Track gains widespread popularity through church groups, community centers, and family gatherings.
Present: Played on custom hand-crafted wooden boards and in digital adaptations.
history.evolution: The transition from dice to cards added strategic depth: players must manage their hand (save high cards vs. play early), timing card usage, and hand-management decisions replace pure chance.
history.cultural: Often played on hand-crafted wooden boards passed down through generations. A staple of inter-generational family gaming, church socials, and community gatherings, particularly in the upper Midwest (Minnesota, Wisconsin) and Canada.

setup.players: 2 to 6 players (can be played in teams with partners sitting opposite each other on a square board).
setup.deck: Each player (or team) has their own full 52-card deck PLUS 2 Jokers (54 cards total per player deck). Keep decks separated by player.
setup.equipment: 1. **Fast Track Board**: Hexagonal or square board with 64-68 spaces around the perimeter plus 4 Home Base centers (one per player/team). 2. **Marbles or Pegs**: 4 marbles per player in their color. 3. **Holding Pen**: Off-board area where marbles start before being entered into play.
setup.dealing: Each player shuffles their own deck and draws 5 cards into their starting hand. Place remaining cards face-down as draw pile.

rules.objective: Be the first player or team to move all 4 marbles from the Holding Pen around the board and into your Home Base (center area).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Turn Sequence**: On your turn, play one card from your hand to move a marble. Draw one card from your deck to return to 5-card hand (unless the card says 'Play Again'). 2. **Exiting the Pen**: You can only move a marble OUT of the Holding Pen with specific 'Start' cards (Joker, Ace, King, Queen, Jack, or 6). These cards can also move your marble forward that many spaces. 3. **Forward Movement**: Play a card matching its number value. Face cards (K, Q, J) can move 10 spaces or exit the Pen. 4. **Backwards Movement (4s)**: The 4 is unique: play a 4 to move a marble BACKWARD 4 spaces. This is a powerful defensive move. 5. **Split Movement (7s)**: Play a 7 to move a single marble 7 spaces OR split the 7 between two different marbles (e.g., 3+4 or 2+5). 6. **Joker (Trump Card)**: Move a marble to any opponent's exact position (bumping them back to their Holding Pen) OR use as a Start card. Play Again. 7. **Play Again Cards**: Aces, 6s, Face Cards, and Jokers grant an extra turn (draw card, take another turn). 8. **Landing on Fast Track**: If you land exactly on a Fast Track entry space, you may use the central shortcut on your next turn to jump across the board.
keyRules: **Bumping**: If you land exactly on a space occupied by an opponent's marble, that opponent's marble returns to their Holding Pen.
**Fast Track Shortcut**: A dangerous shortcut across the board's center. Easy bumping target but saves many spaces.
**Blocking**: You cannot pass your own marbles. If a marble blocks your path, choose a different marble to move.
**Must Move**: If you have a legal move, you MUST take it, even if disadvantageous.

**Card Values**: 2-10 move forward that many spaces. J, Q, K = 10 spaces or Start. Ace = 1 space or Start. 6 = 6 spaces or Start and Play Again. 4 = Move backward 4 spaces. 7 = Move 7 spaces or split between two marbles. Joker = Trump (bump opponent or Start) + Play Again.
**Home Base Entry**: Only certain positions allow entry into Home Base; marbles must enter from the correct position on the track.

strategy.basic: Prioritize getting all 4 marbles out of the Holding Pen early. Start cards are your most valuable resource. Spread your marbles around the board to reduce risk of multiple bumps.
strategy.intermediate: The Backwards 4 Trick: Use the 4 to move a marble backward into a 'shortcut' position that's only 4-6 spaces from Home Base entry. This converts a long board loop into a quick finish. **Fast Track Risk**: Avoid lingering on Fast Track spaces. Enter only if you can exit immediately.
strategy.advanced: Team Coordination (Partnership Play): Sacrifice your own position to bump an opponent threatening your partner's marble. Use split 7s to advance your partner's marbles if rules allow. **Marble Positioning**: Position marbles to block opponents who are ahead. A strategically placed marble forces opponents into 3+ consecutive turns with bad cards.
tips: Always hold one 'Start' card if you have marbles remaining in the Holding Pen.
Never stay on Fast Track longer than one turnâ€”you're a sitting duck.
If you're far behind, use 4s aggressively to reset opponent positions.
In the endgame with 1-2 marbles left, use face cards conservatively. Save Jokers for critical bumps.
Track opponent hand sizes (do they have cards left to draw ). If an opponent is about to draw their last card, they're vulnerable to being forced into dead turns.

difficulty.easy: Moves the marble closest to finishing; never uses 4s strategically; ignores opponent positions; randomly plays high cards.
difficulty.medium: Uses 4s to enter Home Base area faster. Understands when to 'Play Again' to chain moves. Tracks approximate opponent progress. Occasionally bumps nearby opponents.
difficulty.hard: Simulates all possible marble and card combinations to maximize win probability. Holds Jokers to bump opponents in critical positions. Optimizes 'Split 7s' to maximize board control. Models opponent hand states and card depletion. Recognizes when to sacrifice position for team advantage (in partnership play). Predicts optimal Fast Track usage.

considerations: AI must handle pathfinding across two routes: traditional outer loop and dangerous Fast Track shortcut.
AI must balance immediate win attempts against long-term board control.
AI must track all player hand sizes and predict card availability for future turns.
In partnership play, AI must communicate via play decisions (e.g., intentional bumps signal strategy).

play_card.description: Play a card to move one or two marbles. Card value determines movement type and distance.
play_card.constraints: Card must be playable (legal move must exist). If legal move exists, must be taken.

go_out.reason: Game has no going out mechanic.

engine.deckDescription: One full deck of 52 cards using French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) and standard ranks from ace through king, with no jokers.
engine.suitDescription: French suits: hearts (cœurs), diamonds (carreaux), clubs (trèfles), and spades (piques). Each suit has thirteen cards from ace through king.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranking for a 52-card deck: ace (high or low by context), king, queen, jack, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. Thirteen cards per suit.
engine.dealPattern: Each player draws 5 cards from personal deck; remaining cards form draw pile

notApplicableReasons.meldConfig: Fast Track is a race game; cards move marbles on a board. There is no melding or set-collection mechanic.

synthesis.shortDescription: A high-energy race game combining card-driven movement with strategic bumping, split turns, and a dangerous shortcut through the center.

prompts.human: Welcome to Fast Track! You have 4 marbles to move from your Holding Pen around the board and into your Home Base. Play cards to move them. Save your 6s, Aces, Face Cards, and Jokers for extra turns. Use backwards 4s to shortcut into Home. Most importantly: bump your opponents and send them back to start!
prompts.ai: Game: Fast Track. Each player has own 54-card deck (52+2 Jokers). Goal: Move 4 marbles from Holding Pen around 68-space board into Home Base. Turn sequence: play 1 card to move marble(s), draw 1 card back to hand-size of 5. Card effects: 2-10=move forward that number, J/Q/K=10 or Start, A=1 or Start, 6=6 or Start with Play Again, 4=move backward 4, 7=move 7 OR split between 2 marbles, Joker=bump opponent OR Start with Play Again. Bumping: land exactly on opponent = they return to Holding Pen. Fast Track: central shortcut, risky but saves spaces. Play Again: granted by 6, A, Face Cards, Joker = extra turn.

scoring.description: Winner determined by first player/team to place all 4 marbles in Home Base.
scoring.winCondition: First player or team to move all 4 marbles from Holding Pen, around the track, and into Home Base.

penalties.Bumped: Marble returns to Holding Pen, losing all forward progress.
penalties.Blocked: Cannot move forward through own marble; must choose different marble.

scoring.splitRules: 7s can be split between two marbles (e.g., move one marble 3 spaces and another 4 spaces).

nullReasons.targetScore: Game does not use target score mechanic.
